categories.label: Tail lights
notes: Mid-generation facelifts usually restyle the lenses — match the donor to your car's pre- or post-facelift years, not just the generation.

categories.label: Headlights
notes: Mid-generation facelifts usually restyle the housings, and halogen, HID and LED units don't swap — match the donor to your car's facelift years and lamp type.

categories.label: Engine assembly
notes: Same family = the long block interchanges. Manifolds, mounts, oil pan, accessories and wiring often differ between models — plan to swap yours over.
Mileage and internal condition are unknown — yards track cars, not engines. Pull a valve cover or check the oil before you commit.
Engine pulls take hours and need a hoist — call ahead. Some self-serve yards don't allow engine pulls or rent hoists; most charge a core fee refunded on your old unit.

categories.label: Ignition coils
notes: Match the coil part number — coil packs changed within engine families; pull the set, singles age together.

categories.label: Automatic transmission
notes: ALWAYS verify the transmission code on the case tag — ratios, bellhousing and TCM calibration differ even within one model year. Same model + same engine is a starting point, never a guarantee.
Mileage and internal condition are unknown — yards track cars, not transmissions. Check the fluid before you commit.
Transmission pulls take hours — call ahead; most yards charge a refundable core fee.
categories.rowWarn: verify the trans code on the case tag before pulling

categories.label: ECM / PCM (engine computer)
notes: Match the ECM part number exactly — calibrations differ by engine/trans/emissions package, and most 2000s+ cars need the module programmed or married to the immobilizer before they'll start.
categories.rowWarn: match the part number exactly; plan on programming

categories.label: Radio / infotainment
notes: Many factory radios are VIN-locked or anti-theft coded — they may demand a code or dealer pairing in your car. Same model and generation is the only honest fit claim for electronics; options and screens vary by trim.

categories.label: Front seats (pair)
notes: Many 2000s+ front seats contain seat-mounted side airbags — those can't be listed on eBay; local sale or own-car use only.
Match cloth/leather, power/manual and heated options — harness plugs differ by trim.
categories.rowWarn: check for a side-airbag tag on the seat frame

categories.label: Front door
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint — check the door-jamb sticker on both cars. Glass, regulator and harness come along on most yard pulls; power vs manual must match.
categories.rowWarn: match the paint code on the door-jamb sticker

categories.label: Fender
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint — check the door-jamb sticker on both cars. Facelifts sometimes change fender cutlines mid-generation; hold it up before you buy.
categories.rowWarn: match the paint code on the door-jamb sticker

categories.label: Hood
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint — check the door-jamb sticker on both cars. Scoops/vents are trim-specific — match yours.
categories.rowWarn: match the paint code on the door-jamb sticker

categories.label: Front bumper
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint. Park-sensor and fog-light cutouts differ by trim — count the holes before you pull.

categories.label: Grille
notes: Mid-cycle facelifts change grilles while the generation continues — match your car's front clip year, not just the generation.

categories.label: Trunk lid / decklid
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint. Spoiler holes, camera and badge cutouts differ by trim — check the underside before you pull.
categories.rowWarn: match the paint code on the door-jamb sticker

categories.label: Liftgate / hatch
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint. Glass, wiper and camera variants differ within a generation — match yours before pulling.

categories.label: Intake manifold
notes: Manifolds split WITHIN engine families — California-emissions cars, drive-by-wire vs cable-throttle years and upper vs lower plenum designs use different castings on otherwise-identical engines. Match the casting/part number before buying.
Composite (plastic) manifolds crack and warp with age — check the gasket faces and vacuum fittings before you pull.
categories.rowWarn: match the manifold casting/part number — emissions package and throttle type split manifolds within a family

categories.label: Air intake / airbox
notes: Airboxes are usually engine-specific within a generation — match your engine size, and move your MAF/IAT sensor and a fresh filter over before installing.

categories.label: Rear door
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint — check the door-jamb sticker on both cars. Rear doors never interchange with fronts, and sedan vs extended-cab vs crew-cab rear doors differ within one generation.
categories.rowWarn: match the paint code on the door-jamb sticker

categories.label: Rear bumper
notes: Color code must match or plan to paint. Park-sensor and tow-hitch cutouts differ by trim — count the holes before you pull.
